channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Jensen Huang Exit Sets Up US-China Showdown Over AI Chip Curbs
item.description: The fall of Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang has removed the industry’s most prominent opponent of US chip controls, setting up a showdown over potential new curbs that could accelerate China’s drive for semiconductor self-sufficiency.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Talks on SpaceX-Tesla Deal Said to Advance
item.description: SpaceX and Tesla are progressing in their merger negotiations, setting the stage for a combination that could redefine the limits of global dealmaking. Elon Musk’s two largest companies could announce what would be the biggest-ever deal as soon as in December, according to people familiar with the matter. Bloomberg's Manuel Baigorri has more. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Microsoft Outage Gums Up Markets, Forces Traders to Use Phones
item.description: Microsoft Outlook went dark on Rita Elkazzi just as a volatile week in markets was coming to an end. As swings in AI stocks and bonds kept traders on edge, the UBS Group AG execution-sales head for Australia and New Zealand was forced onto phones and alternative channels to communicate.
item.dc:creator: Ruth Carson, Bernadette Toh and Matthew Burgess

item.title: Anthropic IPO Said to Be Six Times Oversubscribed
item.description: Anthropic's initial public offering has drawn about six times the orders for the shares available, according to people familiar with the matter, as interest increases for potentially the biggest first-time share sale ever. The Claude AI model firm and its co-founders are seeking to raise as much as $64.4 billion in the IPO and $26 billion in a private placement, its filings show. Taken together, the offering would be bigger than SpaceX’s IPO, making it the biggest listing of all time. Bloomberg's David Savage reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia CEO Search: Who Are the Candidates for Permanent Role?
item.description: Nvidia is searching for a permanent replacement for larger-than-life Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang, a daunting challenge at the world’s most valuable chipmaker. The company has tapped an outside firm to identify potential candidates following revelations of multiple extramarital affairs by Huang. Longtime Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress is serving as interim CEO. Bloomberg's Tom Mackenzie has more details. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Banned Nvidia Chips Installed at China Data Center Linked to Alice Huang
item.description: A Chinese company founded by Alice Huang, the woman at the center of a controversy dogging Nvidia Corp., procured smuggled AI chips that were installed at a Shanghai data center with links to Megaspeed International Pte, according to documents reviewed by Bloomberg News.
item.dc:creator: Andy Lin, Mackenzie Hawkins and Kari Lindberg

item.title: Analyst Sees Stricter US Export Controls After Nvidia
item.description: Anna Ashton, Founder of Ashton Analytics, says the Nvidia controversy will likely result in stricter US export controls toward China and deepen restrictions on technology products. She speaks on "Bloomberg: The China Show". (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: ByteDance Plans $6 Billion Buyback at $400 Billion Valuation
item.description: ByteDance Ltd. plans to buy back up to $6 billion of shares from investors at a valuation of about $400 billion, marking a 20% uptick from a similar program a year ago, according to people who’ve reviewed the proposal.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Nvidia Sees Record Open Retail Buy After CEO Ousted, Vanda Says
item.description: Retail investors are clinging to hopes of Nvidia Corp.’s rebound, stepping in with aggressive buying after Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang was ousted.
item.dc:creator: Winnie Hsu and David Savage

item.title: Malaysia Intensifies Investigation Into Megaspeed Chips
item.description: Malaysia said it is examining whether AI chips brought into the country by a unit of Singapore-based Megaspeed International Pte were subsequently shipped overseas, tightening scrutiny around a company at the center of the scandal that led to the resignation of Nvidia Corp.’s Jensen Huang.
item.dc:creator: Kok Leong Chan and Danial Azhar

item.title: Singtel CFO on 1H Earnings
item.description: Arthur Lang, Singtel Group CFO, discusses the outlook and growth strategy for the business after the company's first half earnings, and on potential business impact from Nvidia leadership changes. He speaks with Haidi Stroud-Watts and Paul Allen on "Bloomberg: The Asia Trade". (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Singapore Charges Fifth Person as Nvidia Case Expands
item.description: Singapore charged a fifth person in a fraud case linked to the export of computer hardware suspected of containing Nvidia Corp. chips subject to US trade restrictions.
item.dc:creator: Philip J. Heijmans and Gao Yuan

item.title: China Chipmaker SigmaStar Said to Plan $300 Million HK Listing
item.description: SigmaStar Technology Ltd., a Chinese artificial intelligence chipmaker, is seeking to raise as much as $300 million in a Hong Kong listing as soon as this year, people familiar with the matter said, as the nation’s technology companies look for an opportune fundraising window.
item.dc:creator: Sangmi Cha

item.title: Berkshire Pays More to Borrow in Japan on ¥182 Billion Deal
item.description: Berkshire Hathaway Inc. paid more to borrow in Japan than it did in April, with spreads wider across several maturities of its ¥182.3 billion ($1.1 billion) bond sale.
item.dc:creator: Takahiko Hyuga

item.title: Trump Says Huang Told Him He Regrets Scandal’s Toll on Family
item.description: President Donald Trump said Jensen Huang called him and expressed remorse over what the scandal that led to his resignation as chief executive of Nvidia Corp. had done to his family.
item.dc:creator: Hadriana Lowenkron and John Harney

item.title: Inside Jensen Huang's Final Hours as the CEO of Nvidia
item.description: At the end, Jensen Huang looked broken and shattered, his legendary energy depleted. After weeks spent denying the allegations of infidelity and fighting to remain in his job as Nvidia Corp.’s chief executive officer, his surrender late Wednesday night was unconditional. Huang’s usual take-charge demeanor had evaporated, according to a person familiar with the situation, and he’d started using phrases like “whatever” and “I don’t care.”
item.dc:creator: Drake Bennett and Ian King

item.title: Samsung Is in Talks to Acquire Data Center Cooling Firm Modine
item.description: Samsung Electronics Co. is in talks to acquire Modine Manufacturing Co., a maker of cooling systems for data centers, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: David Carnevali and Ryan Gould

item.title: Microsoft Races to Fix Outlook After One of Longest Outages
item.description: Microsoft Corp. is struggling to restore access to its flagship software half a day after an outage began, leaving users unable to access email and chat services in one of the tech giant’s most severe disruptions in recent memory.
item.dc:creator: Matt Day and Mark Anderson

item.title: ‘Dark Day’: Silicon Valley Mourns Nvidia’s Decision to Oust CEO
item.description: The ouster of Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang has sent shockwaves throughout Silicon Valley, prompting a chorus of venture capitalists and founders to criticize the chipmaker’s decision and express concerns about the broader impact on the industry. Huang was removed by Nvidia’s board of directors, two people familiar with the matter said, after reports of two affairs, including one with a woman suspected of spying for China and another with an employee. item.title: Jensen Huang Removed as Nvidia CEO Following Affairs, Board Appoints Kress
item.description: Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang, the preeminent face of the AI infrastructure boom, was ousted from his post after reports of three affairs, including one with a woman suspected of spying for China.
item.dc:creator: Ian King
